statement:
Show that
$$\cos\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\alpha}{4}\right)=\frac{\sin\alpha}{4\sin\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{4}\right)},$$
where $\alpha\neq k\pi$, $k$ an integer.

Prove that, for such $\alpha$,
$$\cos\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\alpha}{4}\right)\cdots\cos\left(\frac{\alpha}{2^n}\right)=\frac{\sin\alpha}{2^n\sin\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2^n}\right)},$$
where $n$ is a positive integer.

Deduce that
$$\alpha=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{4}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{8}\right)\cdots},$$
and hence that
$$\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\tfrac12}\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12}}\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12}}}\cdots}.$$
solution:
Using $\sin 2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ twice:
$$\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{4}=\frac{\sin\alpha}{2\sin(\alpha/2)}\cdot\frac{\sin(\alpha/2)}{2\sin(\alpha/4)}=\frac{\sin\alpha}{4\sin(\alpha/4)}.$$

More generally, the product telescopes:
$$\prod_{k=1}^{n}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2^k}=\prod_{k=1}^{n}\frac{\sin(\alpha/2^{k-1})}{2\sin(\alpha/2^k)}=\frac{\sin\alpha}{2^n\sin(\alpha/2^n)},$$
since each intermediate $\sin(\alpha/2^k)$ cancels.

Letting $n\to\infty$, we have $2^n\sin(\alpha/2^n)\to\alpha$ (as $\sin x/x\to1$), so
$$\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2^k}=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\alpha}.$$
Rearranging,
$$\alpha=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\cos(\alpha/2)\cos(\alpha/4)\cos(\alpha/8)\cdots}.$$

For $\alpha=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, using the half-angle values $\cos\tfrac{\pi}{4}=\sqrt{\tfrac12}$, $\cos\tfrac{\pi}{8}=\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12}}$, and so on (each from $\cos\tfrac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\tfrac{1+\cos\theta}{2}}$), we obtain
$$\frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\tfrac12}\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12}}\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12+\tfrac12\sqrt{\tfrac12}}}\cdots}.$$
